name: Noticed
tagline: No score, no leaderboard, on purpose.
summary: A shared board for the invisible labour of running a household. Log what you notice needs doing — no category, no assignee, no due date — and see it side by side once a week with what your partner noticed.

authorship.role: Sole author — product model, identity model and weekly comparison view.
built: The single-field capture flow and the deliberately neutral weekly comparison
The join-code household model with no accounts and device-local identity
notBuilt: Supabase Realtime, which carries the shared board state

caseStudy.problem: The driver of household resentment is usually not unfinished chores but unequal noticing — remembering the appointment needs booking or the shoes no longer fit. Chore-split apps track completed tasks and miss the anticipatory work entirely. And every shared household app dies the same way: logging becomes more effort than just doing the thing.
caseStudy.approach: Two constraints, both of which cost features. Capture is a single text field with no required category, assignee or due date, because anything slower than a few seconds defeats the purpose. And the weekly view shows noticed and resolved counts side by side, framed neutrally — no fairness percentage, no ranking — because a scoreboard turns the tool into ammunition in an argument.

visuals.alt: Illustration of a shared board with two columns of noticed items
visuals.caption: Illustration of the weekly side-by-side view. Not a screenshot — no capture of the running app has been published yet.

outcomes.statement: There are no user accounts at all — a household is a short join code, and each person's name and colour are stored locally on their own device.

tradeoffs.choice: Join code as the entire identity model
tradeoffs.gained: A household is usable in under a minute, with no sign-up friction for the partner who did not choose the app.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: The join code is the only thing protecting the board, which the project's own README documents as a security limitation rather than glossing over.

tradeoffs.gained: The tool makes invisible work visible without giving either person a number to win with.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: The engagement mechanics that would make it stickier are exactly the ones that would make it harmful here.

lessons: Some products are defined by what you refuse to add. A fairness percentage would have been trivial to compute and would have changed what the app is for.
limitations: No external pentest; RLS isolation is exercised by the integration suite only.
Invitation tokens are hashed but brute-force resistance is not load-tested.
Two-person scope is a product decision, not an enforced guarantee — any household member sees everything.
